severe_claims.claim_text: Material weakness in internal controls over financial reporting (KPMG adverse opinion as of Dec 31, 2025). Net loss of $226.6M on $335.4M revenue in 2025. $94.5M cash + $35M revolver capacity; $88.4M JPMorgan term loan + $47.1M convertible preferred. Net EAC adjustments swung from -$17.7M (2024) to -$54.5M (2025). ATM-financed equity issuance of $518.4M in 2025.

key_atm_prospectus_supplements: 2025-11-10 ATM filing-fee exhibit + ATM prospectus supp

severe_claims.interpretation: Severe distress / quality-of-earnings markers per heuristic 10. KPMG issued an adverse opinion on internal control over financial reporting as of Dec 31, 2025. Two distinct material weaknesses identified (process-level controls; IT general controls). Net loss expanded to $226.6M (-68% operating margin) on $335.4M revenue. EAC unfavorable adjustments are accelerating year-over-year (-$3.5M -> -$17.7M -> -$54.5M) which is a forensic indicator of contract pricing/estimating problems. The 5% gross margin (vs 15% prior year) is barely positive after $13.6M Edge purchase-accounting inventory adjustment. Cash burn from operations was $177M. The company funded itself almost entirely via dilution — $518.4M of ATM/equity issuance in 2025, with at least four distinct 424B5 prospectus supplements (May 2026 already filing more ATM capacity). Convertible preferred PIK dividends (8,068 + 3,312 shares of preferred-on-preferred) plus a $63.9M repurchase from Bain Capital are mezzanine-equity churn. JPM Term loan refi extending out to 2029 was a Subsequent Event (Feb 2026). Combined: material-weakness + adverse opinion + accelerating EAC + heavy ATM dilution + preferred PIK = SEVERE per heuristic 10. (Going-concern language not present, hence not RED_FLAG.) SEVERE.

moderate_claims.claim_text: Redwire is the prime mission integrator on DARPA's Otter VLEO air-breathing satellite program using its SabreSat platform, and Phantom is being used on ESA's Skimsat VLEO program.
moderate_claims.M_check: usaspending DoD contracts + edgar_fts SabreSat asymmetric-mention test
moderate_claims.interpretation: Partial corroboration. DoD aggregate ($70.4M, 12 awards) supports the general defense relationship, but the SPECIFIC DARPA Otter prime-integrator contract does not appear in USAspending awards under DARPA-labeled awarding sub-agency or with 'Otter / VLEO / air-breathing' keywords in descriptions. The top DoD awards are AFRL space-structures programs (CALL 002 ASSIST, SCARLET, ELLI), not DARPA Otter. DARPA prime-integrator awards at $-millions normally ARE in USAspending under 'Department of Defense'; absence here is mild evidence of either (a) Otter being a very recent OTA award not yet reflected, or (b) Redwire being a sub on someone else's prime. The asymmetric-mention test on SabreSat is also a soft yellow flag: 16 SEC hits but 0 from external filers — entirely Redwire's own 8-K/10-Q. The ESA Skimsat reference is in a foreign-agency jurisdiction (heuristic 5: ESA off-EDGAR) and is UNVERIFIABLE. Net: claim is partially supported by the broader DoD relationship; the specific Otter prime-integrator label is not yet independently verifiable. MODERATE.

moderate_claims.claim_text: Defense Tech segment includes Stalker UAS and Penguin UAS. On July 14, 2025, Stalker UAS was granted Authority to Operate by the DIU and placed on the DIU Blue UAS List. Stalker has 'thousands of flight hours across six continents' with U.S. Marine Corps and U.S. Army customers; Penguin C used by Ukraine Armed Forces, Latvia and Lithuania MoD, Royal Saudi Air Force.
moderate_claims.M_check: usaspending Edge Autonomy + UAV Factory contracts

M_value.Edge_Autonomy_top_award: N0001925P1000 - VXE30 STALKER UAS purchase order ($1.48M)

moderate_claims.interpretation: Mixed corroboration. The acquired Edge Autonomy entity shows just $1.6M of USAspending contracts post-2020 (a single VXE30 STALKER purchase order with the Department of the Navy), plus $61K to legacy UAV Factory (Penguin's original OEM). Foreign sales (Ukraine, Latvia, Lithuania, Saudi) are heuristic-5 off-EDGAR / unverifiable. Stalker's historical USMC/Army deployment heritage predates Edge Autonomy and was largely under Lockheed Martin Skunk Works — making direct USAspending validation difficult under the current entity name. The Edge Autonomy acquisition was just completed June 13, 2025, so the small contract footprint may also reflect entity-name lag in USAspending. The headline-customer claim (USMC, Army) is plausible at the heritage-product level but only $1.5M is independently visible. Penguin C foreign-MoD customers are entirely off-domain. MODERATE — direct evidence is materially below the headline.

moderate_claims.claim_text: Redwire's solar/power systems are flight-deployed on NASA's Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE), NASA's DART, NASA's Artemis I lunar mission, ISS, and Space Force GPS Satellite program. Redwire delivers 'multiple advanced RF payloads for a constellation of satellites for a national security satellite constellation in LEO' (likely Space Development Agency / NRO Proliferated LEO).
moderate_claims.M_check: usaspending USSF/SDA/NRO + edgar_fts LMT/NOC/LHX counterparty disclosure

M_value.NASA_IXPE_DART_visible_in_USAspending: NASA solar/structures contracts visible (IXPE/DART/Artemis ROSA subcontract trails through prime missions)

moderate_claims.interpretation: Mixed. The 'national security satellite constellation in LEO' claim is a vague / unnamed-program reference (likely SDA or NRO Proliferated LEO) and is NOT verifiable in USAspending top-50 awards under either USSF, SDA, or NRO as awarding agency. None of the three defense primes plausibly involved (LMT, NOC, L3Harris) mention Redwire in their SEC filings — heuristic-7 yellow flag, although Redwire's likely subcontract dollars sit below the primes' segment-disclosure materiality thresholds. The NASA missions (IXPE, DART, Artemis I) are supported by Redwire's NASA contract trail (Tipping Point $87M, multiple JSC task orders). The Space Force GPS Satellite program claim flows through Lockheed prime — not directly visible, but consistent with heritage. External all-filer mention count of Redwire is 423 (robust general SEC visibility, presumably analysts + co-investors). Net: NASA-mission claim is well-supported, defense-constellation claim is materially under-corroborated by USAspending. MODERATE.

moderate_claims.claim_text: ASTS has a federal contract with the U.S. Space Development Agency (SDA) — including a $43.0M contract via a prime contractor for testing services using the initial BB satellites, plus a direct $30.0M SDA Europa Track 2 commercial-solutions contract, plus an IDIQ award under the Missile Defense Agency's SHIELD program.
moderate_claims.M_check: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts (AST SPACEMOBILE, AST & Science, AST Space Mobile USA, AST LLC, SpaceMobile, AST Space; both all-agency and DoD-only). DoD-only AST SPACEMOBILE = 0 awards. Best canonical recipient hit = 'AST SPACE MOBILE USA LLC' with only 2 awards total: NASA $969,573 (legacy cubesat bus, ACS3 solar-sail, 2019-vintage award ID 80ARC019P0003) and DoD $500 SHIELD IDIQ stub (HQ085926FF777). No $30M direct SDA Europa Track 2 award visible; no $43M-equivalent obligation visible under the prime-contractor path.
moderate_claims.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic Layer 3 Rule 7 fires. The SHIELD IDIQ existence IS corroborated (a $500 'initial order' under HQ085926DG110 / HQ085926FF777 matches the 10-K's IDIQ disclosure), so the relationship is genuine. The $43M SDA-via-prime contract may legitimately be off-USAspending under ASTS's name because the obligation sits with the prime, so we cannot hard-refute that. HOWEVER the direct $30M SDA Europa Track 2 commercial-solutions contract SHOULD be visible in USAspending and is not — that is a partial contradiction. Net read: relationship-class verified (SHIELD IDIQ exists), but the headline dollar figures ($43M + $30M) are not corroborated at the dollar level on the most authoritative source. MODERATE: claim is stage-true but the dollar magnitudes are not yet observable, and the IDIQ has not produced any obligation beyond $500 as of pull date.

moderate_claims.claim_text: ASTS has 5 Block 1 BB satellites in orbit (launched September 12, 2024) and launched its first Block 2 BB satellite (BB6) on December 23, 2025 — i.e. 6 commercial BB satellites in orbit at cutoff, with claimed near-term plans to initiate limited noncontinuous SpaceMobile service.
moderate_claims.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext: 'BlueBird' = 418 hits 2024-09 to cutoff; 'BlueWalker' = 71 hits 2022 to cutoff. External corroboration of the BlueBird launch narrative is substantial (high mention count across filings). The 10-K itself discloses (Item 1 + financial-statement notes) capitalization of exactly 5 Block 1 BB satellites in property-and-equipment 'satellites in orbit' AND a 6th (BB6, Block 2) launched 2025-12-23 with on-orbit phased-array deployment confirmed February 10, 2026.

M_value.commercial_service_status: not yet launched / zero service revenue

moderate_claims.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational) AND Heuristic 9 (constellation-operational vs constellation-announced) — the 6-satellites-in-orbit count is internally consistent and externally well-mentioned. HOWEVER the much larger constellation (multiple hundreds at design) required for global continuous SpaceMobile commercial service is NOT yet deployed. The 10-K explicitly states 'The SpaceMobile Service has not been launched and therefore has not yet generated any revenue.' Bright-line distinction (Heuristic 3): test-call demo + a handful of operational BBs is real; continuous commercial service is not. MODERATE — claim as stated is technically true but the marketing tier ('definitive commercial agreements / commercial service starting 2026') conflates demonstration capability with operational-network reality. Investors who interpret '6 BB satellites = commercial network online' would be misreading the stage.

moderate_claims.claim_text: ASTS reports $2.8 billion of cash and restricted cash at 12/31/2025 (up from $567.5M at 12/31/2024), reported FY2025 net loss before NCI of approximately $461M; SpaceMobile Service has not been launched and has generated zero service revenue; risk factor explicitly references potential future going-concern qualifier. ASTS has a long history of heavily dilutive financings.
moderate_claims.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext (cik 0001780312): 'going concern' = 10 hits (consistent with persistent risk-factor language; no active GC qualifier flagged in the 10-K's audit opinion section). 'reverse stock split' = 9 hits (consistent with anti-takeover authorization language; no recent split executed). 'ATM' / at-the-market = 35 hits (extensive use of ATM equity-offering programs — classic dilutive financing pattern). 10-K self-reports: cash + restricted cash $2.8B at 12/31/2025 vs $567.5M at 12/31/2024 (i.e. ~$2.3B in net financing inflows over the year); FY2025 net loss before NCI of $461M; zero SpaceMobile service revenue.
moderate_claims.interpretation: Calibration Heuristic 10 (DELISTING / GOING-CONCERN) — the surface looks fine right now: $2.8B cash, no active going-concern qualifier, no recent reverse split. HOWEVER (a) the company has $0 service revenue and a $461M annual loss, with capex still required for the Block 2 production ramp, (b) the financing pattern (35 ATM-related mentions, repeated S-3 ATM filings, and the implied $2.23B 2025 net inflow) is classic 'dilution-funded R&D' — exactly the pattern Heuristic 10 warns about, (c) commentary in the 10-K explicitly preserves the future-going-concern flag. Net: NOT a current distress event, but the financing footprint IS persistent dilutive equity issuance and the next cash refresh round before commercial service ramps is essentially mandatory. MODERATE — claim as stated (current cash position) is accurately disclosed; the dilution-prone capital structure is corroborated and worth flagging.

severe_claims.claim_text: $26.6B total debt / finance lease obligations outstanding (Dec 31, 2024); $53.1B total 5-year long-term obligations including interest; $5.356B 10-3/4% Senior Secured Notes due 2029 issued Nov 2024; $2.5B New DISH DBS Financing from TPG Angelo Gordon at 10.75-11.25% with 13.25-13.75% mandatorily-redeemable preferred; $400M PIPE at $28.04/share including $43.5M from CONX (Ergen-affiliated); DTV terminated DISH DBS sale Nov 22, 2024; $100M related-party backstop on the 10-3/4% notes from a Charles Ergen-related party; $1.819B of 0% Convertible Notes due 2025 + $2.863B of 3-3/8% Convertible Notes due 2026 extinguished in Nov 2024 Exchange Offers.
severe_claims.supports: self-corroborated and confirmed by later filings
severe_claims.M_value: 8 hits for 'going concern' across EchoStar filings — including its 10-Q dated 2025-11-06, 10-Q dated 2025-08-01, FY2025 10-K filed 2026-03-02, and Q1-2026 10-Q filed 2026-05-11. The FY2024 10-K under review does NOT carry a going-concern qualifier, but subsequent quarterly filings in 2025 and the FY2025 10-K filed 2026-03-02 DO carry going-concern language (8 separate filings flagged). The FY2024 10-K's $53.1B 5-year obligation table is internally consistent. Defensive financing at distressed coupons (10.75-11.25% senior secured; 13.25-13.75% preferred), Ergen-related-party $95M of $100M backstop, and CONX (Ergen-affiliated SPAC) participating in the PIPE are all related-party distress patterns. The DTV walk-away from DISH DBS in Nov 2024 indicates the Pay-TV asset was insufficiently attractive for an independent buyer at the proposed terms. Calibration Heuristic 10 (delisting/going-concern) is the relevant frame, and the post-cutoff (relative to FY2024 10-K) reality includes explicit going-concern disclosure.
severe_claims.interpretation: SEVERE. From a Signal OS forward-test posture (cutoff 2026-05-16, FY2024 10-K filed Feb 2025): the financing structure disclosed in this 10-K is already a forensic distress pattern — distressed-pricing senior secured + senior unsecured exchange offers extinguishing par-value convertibles + related-party backstop + buyer (DTV) walking away from the proposed Pay-TV divestiture. The fact that EchoStar's subsequent 8 filings through Q1 2026 carry 'going concern' language is exactly what would be predicted from the FY2024 10-K's leverage profile. This is not a hindsight-only signal — a forensic reader of the FY2024 10-K alone would flag SEVERE distress risk.

moderate_claims.claim_text: $30B+ invested in Wireless spectrum licenses; total carrying amount $38.99B (including $9.5B capitalized interest) as of Dec 31, 2024; FCC Extension Request grants final-deadline extensions from June 14, 2025 to Dec 14, 2026 if Commitments #2 and #3 met (including 24,000 5G sites by June 14, 2025).
moderate_claims.supports: verified financial scale, but contingent build-out is a material risk
moderate_claims.M_value: 7 hits for 'FCC Extension Request' in EchoStar filings; 54 hits for 'Northstar Re-Auction Payment' across DISH/EchoStar filings spanning 2018-2025. Northstar/SNR re-auction overhang is a long-standing AWS-3 disclosure that has not been resolved.
moderate_claims.interpretation: Spectrum investment claim is verifiable and corroborated by capitalized cost on balance sheet ($9.5B capitalized interest specifically suggests aging-asset, not productive return). The FCC Extension Request is a real regulatory event but is itself an EXTENSION of build-out deadlines that have repeatedly slipped — Calibration Heuristic 3 (planned vs operational) applies strongly. The 24,000 5G sites + low-cost-plan + 3GPP Release 17 upgrade obligations are HIGH-stakes conditional milestones on which final spectrum-license validity depends. MODERATE because (a) the asset value is verified by capitalized cost, but (b) the build-out trajectory has historically slipped multiple times and (c) AWS-3 Northstar/SNR re-auction liability remains unquantified and contingent — same disclosure across 7+ years.

moderate_claims.claim_text: Neutron medium-lift vehicle (13,000 kg reusable to LEO) under development at LC-3 Wallops; Jan 21 2026 Stage 1 tank ruptured in hydro qual test, impacting launch schedule; securities class action re Neutron progress representations.

M_value.securities_class_action_status: Motion to Dismiss granted Nov 10 2025; amended complaint filed Dec 19 2025; second MTD filed Jan 19 2026
M_value.lc3_status: expected in service in 2026; under construction

moderate_claims.interpretation: MODERATE per Calibration Heuristic 3 (planned-vs-operational with EXTRA WEIGHT). Neutron is squarely in the 'design/prototype' stage of the stage ladder — not yet first-launched. The Jan 2026 tank rupture is candidly disclosed as a subsequent event, and the 8-K trail confirms timely public disclosure. However, the existence of a securities class action specifically alleging misstatements about Neutron development progress is a real signal that prior public communications may have overstated readiness; the case had survived to amended-complaint stage as of cutoff. Score MODERATE because: (a) the 10-K itself is honest about the slip; (b) the still-pending litigation indicates the market is testing the prior optimism; (c) Neutron 2026 service entry now looks optimistic given Q1 tank failure. Not SEVERE because disclosure is contemporaneous and concrete.

moderate_claims.claim_text: Remaining performance obligations of $852.4M as of Jan 31, 2026; ~34% to be recognized within 12 months, ~65% within 24 months.
moderate_claims.supports: RPO is a GAAP-disclosed audited number — auditor-attested per ASC 606. The $852M backlog is substantial relative to $307.7M FY2026 revenue (~2.8x). However: (a) only 34% (~$290M) is expected within 12 months, only modestly above FY2026 actual ($307.7M), implying FLAT near-term growth absent new bookings; (b) the SwAF deal (low 9-figure ~$100M+) is largely milestone-based and back-end-loaded; (c) satellite-services revenue under cost-to-cost has cumulative-catch-up risk if cost estimates change. No SEC-filer counterparty corroboration of $852M backlog is available because key customers are foreign governments/IC.
moderate_claims.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext('Planet Labs') across major US-listed counterparties (T, LMT, BA, AMZN)

moderate_claims.interpretation: RPO is a real GAAP number, but the lack of counterparty corroboration in US-listed defense primes is consistent with PL's customer base being non-US-filer governments (Sweden, NATO, Ukraine, IC). MODERATE rather than PASS because Heuristic 9 (constellation-operational vs announced) applies: a meaningful share of the RPO depends on the SwAF Pelican constellation, which is at the SIGNED-not-OPERATIONAL stage. Stage-ladder execution risk on milestone-based satellite-services revenue is real.
